subject: EpsilonAI request: tailored session-log retention & SIG/CAIQ evidence
messages:
From: Sam Hargreaves <sam.hargreaves@epsilonai.com>
To: Priya Natarajan <priya_natarajan@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Cc: EpsilonAI Security <security+compliance@epsilonai.com>
Date: Tue, 20 Jul 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Request: longer session/debug log retention for EpsilonAI tenant (SIG/CAIQ evidence needed)

Hi Priya / Marissa,

We have an incoming regulatory review (financial services customer) and the auditor is asking that session-level debug traces for our tenant be retained for 180 days rather than the default 30 days. The ask is narrow: only session/debug traces (not full PII payloads) and scoped to our tenant environment.

Two quick asks:
1) Can Redwood support a tenant-scoped retention change to 180 days for debug/session logs?
2) For our SIG/CAIQ submission we need an evidence packet (control mapping + copies of retention config, export proof-of-delete, and an attestation path). Can you outline what artifacts Redwood can provide and whether any manual steps or signed approvals will be required?

Target date for our auditor is Aug 1 — I know that's tight. Attaching our auditor's checklist (excerpt).

Thanks,
Sam

Attachments: Epsilon_Auditor_Checklist_excerpt.pdf (attached)

From: Priya Natarajan <priya_natarajan@redwood.com>
To: Sam Hargreaves <sam.hargreaves@epsilonai.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 20 Jul 2027 10:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: longer session/debug log retention for EpsilonAI tenant (SIG/CAIQ evidence needed)

Sam — thanks for the clear ask and the timeline. Short answer: yes, we can support a tenant-scoped increase to 180 days for session/debug traces, with a few controls and an internal approval path.

I've attached an initial Retention-Matrix and a SIG-Evidence-Index that maps the artifacts we can produce to common SIG/CAIQ questions. High-level notes:
- Scope: session/debug traces only (we will exclude full message payloads and any token-level content flagged as PII).
- Isolation: logs will be retained in a tenant-scoped S3 bucket (encrypted with customer-derived keys / KMS namespace) and access will be limited to our forensic-runbook role.
- Evidence: we can export retention config (policy JSON), a sample export showing retention timestamps, and an operations attestation signed by our Security manager.
- Controls gaps/impacts: this will require a change to our retention automation and an Ops-runbook update; we should expect a 7–10 day turnaround for the implementation once we have approvals.

Next steps I propose:
1) Internal feasibility/controls review (Irene + Eng) — today
2) Draft runbook + evidence list — by Thu (22 Jul)
3) Signed attestation and DPA redline coordination — target Mon (26 Jul)

If Aug 1 is hard, please flag which artifacts are mandatory vs nice-to-have for the auditor. We will treat the export proof-of-delete and policy JSON as first priority.

Best,
Priya Natarajan
Sr. Security & Compliance Manager
Redwood Inference

Attachments: Retention-Matrix.pdf, SIG-Evidence-Index.xlsx

From: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.com>
To: Priya Natarajan <priya_natarajan@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 20 Jul 2027 14:30:00 -0700
Subject: INTERNAL: feasibility notes — EpsilonAI 180-day session-log retention

Team — quick internal assessment (ops/infra implications):

Summary: technically feasible with tenant-scoped retention policy and role-limited access. Key bullets:
- Implementation: update our log-retention microservice to accept tenant-level overrides and create a tenant-dedicated S3 prefix with lifecycle 180d.
- Encryption/keys: recommend customer-scoped KMS key namespace; if the customer demands customer-managed keys (CMK/HSM) that adds procurement steps.
- Access controls: create a "forensics-read" IAM role limited to the retention bucket; require approval workflow (ticket in PagerDuty or ServiceNow) to elevate access.
- SIG/CAIQ artifacts we can produce programmatically: retention_policy.json (with timestamps), S3 object metadata listing with retention TTLs, bucket ACLs & encryption config, and an operations attestation template.
- Evidence that will require manual curation: redacted sample export (to remove tokens), signed attestation PDF, and any DPA redlines.

Risk/cost: modest S3 storage delta (estimate +3–6% for customers with heavy debug traces). We'll track cost to the deal and route to Finance to add to the Dedicated/Reserved proposal if needed.

I attached extraction notes for CAIQ mapping and a sample commands list we'll run to generate the proof-of-delete evidence. Also: we should confirm whether the auditor will accept a partial export (sample) vs full retention index.

Irene
Senior Infrastructure Security Engineer

Attachments: CAIQ-Extraction-Notes.txt

From: Maya Patel <maya.patel@epsilonai.com>

Cc: Sam Hargreaves <sam.hargreaves@epsilonai.com>, EpsilonAI Security <security+compliance@epsilonai.com>
Date: Thu, 22 Jul 2027 09:41:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: longer session/debug log retention for EpsilonAI tenant (SIG/CAIQ evidence needed)

Priya — thanks for the quick reply and the matrix. We reviewed the attachments with our compliance team and are broadly aligned with the proposed scope. Two follow-ups: 

1) Can you produce a short runbook we can include in the CAIQ response (steps for a forensic export + verification commands)? Sam indicated the auditor needs the exact CLI/API calls.
2) We'll need a redline to the DPA for the retention exception (we'll send our proposed language). Can you identify who on your legal/compliance side will shepherd DPA redlines?

If you can get the runbook + evidence index by Thursday (22 Jul) that'll be ideal — the auditor will accept a sample export for now, they want to see the mechanism and controls for proof-of-delete. Also can you share a DocuSign stub for the attestation so we can route internally?

Thanks — attaching our proposed DPA excerpt (redlines).
